title: handoff.py FreshnessState.from_cbor_map lacks type validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Lines: 236-247

FreshnessState.from_cbor_map() extracts fields from CBOR without validating their types:

```python
return cls(
    sequence=data["seq"],
    active_until=data.get("active"),
    retain_until=data["retain"],
    updated_at=data["updated"],
)
```

Expected types:
- sequence: int
- active_until: float | None
- retain_until: float
- updated_at: float

If malformed CBOR provides wrong types (e.g., a string for sequence), the dataclass stores them without error. Issues manifest later when the values are used (e.g., arithmetic on non-numeric sequence).

Compare to OscoreState.from_cbor_map() which validates integer bounds and types carefully (lines 189-197).

Fix: Add type checks before construction:
```python
if not isinstance(data["seq"], int):
    raise HandoffError("sequence must be integer")
if not isinstance(data["retain"], (int, float)):
    raise HandoffError("retain_until must be numeric")
# etc.
```

Impact: Defense in depth; malformed handoff responses could cause unexpected exceptions instead of clean rejection.
